overview: This file documents American efforts between 1932 and 1937 to obtain access to Japanese imperial ceremonies, garden parties, palaces, and audiences. Correspondence among legislators, the State Department, the American Embassy in Tokyo, consular officials, travelers, and Japanese authorities reveals a carefully regulated system in which invitations to the imperial Cherry Blossom and Chrysanthemum parties remained under Japanese control, while visits to the Kyoto Imperial Palace could be facilitated through the Embassy. The records also cover restrictions on consular attendance, ceremonial planning for a congressional delegation, and diplomatic refusals to pursue exceptional access for private citizens and journalists.
interest: Americans seeking imperial-garden and palace privileges, and how State, Embassy and Japanese authorities decided who merited access or an audience.
